Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody thanks for taking the time, um this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. quick intro round?
[00:08] Marcus: yeah Marcus here, head of ML at Valen IO. we're building a realtime conversational assistant for enterprise docs, heavy context, 8k–16k tokens, need real-time answers.
[00:17] Rita: Rita, infra/SRE. i'll be worried about throughput and burst patterns, security, compliance.
[00:22] Samir: Samir, CTO. main ask is predictable latency and cost — ideally p95 sub-300ms for single-turn responses, and decent streaming when we do multi-turn followups.
[00:31] Priya: thanks. just to clarify, when you say p95 sub-300ms is that end-to-end or decode latency?
[00:36] Samir: end-to-end, user to first token in streaming, for short prompts (~300 tokens) we want that p95 target. for longer generations we're more flexible but p95 should stay under 800ms for up to 1024 tokens.
[00:48] Marcus: concurrency: typically 200 concurrent users during peak, with spiky batches up to 800 for launches. sustained throughput target is around 1500 tokens/sec overall, but important is per-request latency when under concurrency.
[01:01] Jordan: ok got it. that aligns with a lot of customers looking at hosted vs dedicated. Priya, want to take the latency/infra side?
[01:06] Priya: sure. high level: Redwood hosted can usually meet sub-300ms p95 for lighter models and optimized kernels on GPU pools, but for strict, predictable SLAs customers often go Dedicated — reserved GPU pools — or Private if they need VPC/on-prem for compliance. For p95 <300ms at 200–800 concurrency, dedicated instances with consistent warm KV cache and batching configs are typical.
[01:28] Rita: when you say KV cache warming — how do you handle cold starts? our traffic is spiky and we can't tolerate big latency cliffs.
[01:35] Priya: good question. we do intelligent pre-warming and prefix caching. cold starts come from model instance spin-up; Dedicated lets you keep warm workers pinned. Hosted has burst capacity but cold starts can add 500ms–2s depending on model and infra. we also offer autoscaling policies with warm buffer, and you can configure min-replicas.
[01:51] Marcus: can you give numbers — e.g., token/sec on A100/4080, and p95 for 13B-class model?
[01:58] Priya: for a 13B open checkpoint on A100 80GB, you can expect around 1800–2200 tokens/sec in optimal batching, single-request decode latency p50 ~80–120ms, p95 depends on concurrency and batch mix — often 200–400ms in Dedicated with tuned batching. On 4080/RTX series it's lower, like 600–900 tokens/sec. but this is very model and prompt specific.
[02:19] Marcus: ok, and for streaming — do you do chunked-first-token semantics? we need first token fast then follow-on tokens streamed at stable token/sec.
[02:27] Priya: yes streaming is supported. we can prioritize first-token latency by using smaller initial decode steps and then larger batching for subsequent tokens. we measure both first-token p95 and streaming throughput (tokens/sec) per worker.
[02:36] Samir: what's the tradeoff between quantization and latency? we want lower memory footprint but don't want to lose p95.
[02:41] Priya: quantization reduces memory and can increase throughput but sometimes slightly increases decode latency due to dequantization steps — in practice int8 or awq profiles are a good compromise. Redwood Optimize helps recommend quant profile by workload.
[02:54] Rita: security questions — data residency, KMS, audit logs — we're in regulated space. does Redwood Private give full KMS control?
[03:00] Jordan: yes Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs. we can run in your VPC or on-prem, and we have SOC 2 report — we'll share docs.
[03:09] Marcus: great. if we do Private, will performance be identical to Dedicated/Hosted?
[03:14] Priya: performance depends on your hardware choices and network topology. Private with customer GPU (A100 NVLink cluster) can match Dedicated if configured similarly. we do kernel selection and runtime optimizations but the base HW and NICs matter.
[03:27] Jordan: any constraint on model weights leaving your environment?
[03:30] Samir: we need to ensure model weights never leave our VPC.
[03:33] Priya: Private addresses that: control plane can be customer-managed and model artifacts can be stored in customer S3 with no egress.
[03:39] Marcus: on benchmarking — we want to run token/sec tests and p95 under synthetic and real prompts. can Redwood run benchmarks in Dedicated and Private?
[03:46] Priya: yes, we can run both. typical approach: we agree on a sample prompt set (you provide 50–200 prompts representative of production), we run steady-state concurrency, and measure first-token p95, end-to-end p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. we also do streaming tests for first-token and sustained tokens/sec.
[04:05] Rita: what about network egress latency — our users are in EU; does region matter?
[04:09] Priya: yes region matters. Hosted has multi-region and low network lat; Dedicated can be provisioned in EU region, Private obviously within your infra. latency to user matters for end-to-end p95.
[04:18] Marcus: how do you instrument traces? we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns to correlate regressions.
[04:23] Jordan: Redwood Console gives token-level breakdowns, per-route traces, and we can attach tracing hooks. plus you can export logs to your SIEM.
[04:30] Samir: competitors — we've tested Anthropic and OpenAI endpoints; cost is high for sustained volume. also looking at self-hosting with Weaviate for embeddings.
[04:37] Jordan: makes sense. Redwood Optimize aims to reduce unit cost via batching and caching without large quality loss.
[04:43] Marcus: quick nit: transcription — sorry, question on p95 under 800 concurrency — you said Dedicated can handle 200–800 with pinned workers. what's the rough number of A100s we'd need?
[04:52] Priya: rough back-of-envelope: for a 13B LLM if you want 800 concurrent short-chat requests with p95 <300ms, you may need ~8–12 A100s depending on batching and average token length. we'll do a more precise capacity planning after we see your prompt distribution and token lengths.
[05:07] Rita: can Redwood run a PoC where we push our traffic profile and you reproduce p95 and tokens/sec so we can compare hosted vs dedicated vs our private cluster?
[05:14] Priya: absolutely. typical PoC includes a 2–4 week benchmark window, we run tests in a dedicated environment and provide dashboards. Private PoC takes a bit more setup but we can run the same tests.
[05:24] Marcus: timeline — we want to decide by end of Q1. pilot in January, production by March.
[05:30] Jordan: sounds doable. we'll put together a proposal and cost estimates.
[05:33] Samir: question on billing — do you bill for warm replicas? we don't want pods idling incurring huge cost.
[05:38] Jordan: Dedicated has reserved capacity with commit levels; we can model cost both with and without warm buffers. there's also autoscaling with min-replicas and burst capacity.
[05:47] Marcus: one more: model versioning and rollouts. we need canarying and automatic fallback if a new model has quality regression.
[05:53] Priya: Redwood supports rollouts, A/B tests, canarying and automatic fallback policies. you can tie quality monitoring to prompt sets/evals to detect regression.
[06:02] Rita: network controls: SAML SSO, RBAC?
[06:05] Jordan: yes SAML/SSO, RBAC, org-level roles. we'll include the compliance checklist in the docs.
[06:11] Marcus: ok that's helpful. do you have any known issues with tokenization mismatches when customers bring custom tokenizers?
[06:16] Priya: sometimes, yes — tokenization differences can cause prompt length variance and latency shifts. we recommend standardizing tokenizers and we'll add that to the benchmark checklist.
[06:25] Samir: great. can you share a sample benchmark report you've done for customers with similar profile?
[06:29] Jordan: yes we'll share a redacted benchmark PDF and a sample dashboard.
[06:33] Marcus: anything else on SLAs? we need p99 availability commitments for production.
[06:37] Jordan: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and we can discuss contractual terms for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has standard terms for self-serve.
[06:44] Priya: and for the PoC we'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and cost, and show cost per 1M tokens across configs.
[06:52] Marcus: ok let's recap.
[06:54] Jordan: recap: 1) Jordan to send pricing and Dedicated vs Hosted breakdown incl. options for warm buffer modeling. 2) Priya to share SOC2, architecture checklist, and sample benchmark reports. 3) Marcus to provide representative prompt set (50–200 prompts) and traffic profile. 4) Schedule benchmark run week of 2026-12-14 for initial results, PoC plan for Jan.
[07:18] Rita: yep, i'll be on the setup calls for infra.
[07:21] Samir: thanks everyone.
[07:23] Jordan: thanks all we'll follow up in email with the docs and next steps.
